verses.text: Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread were two days away. The chief priests and legal teachers were looking for a sneaky way to arrest Jesus and kill him.
They said, “Not during the festival. The people might riot.”

While Jesus was in Bethany at Simon the leper’s house, he was reclining at the table. A woman came with an alabaster jar of very expensive pure nard perfume. She broke the jar and poured it over his head.
Some people there got angry and said to each other, “Why waste that perfume?
“It could’ve been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor!” They were harsh with her.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. Why are you giving her a hard time? She’s done something good for me.
“You’ll always have the poor with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you won’t always have me.
“She did what she could. She poured perfume on my body ahead of time to prepare it for burial.
“I’m telling you the truth: wherever the good news is preached throughout the world, people will also remember what she did.”
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
They were glad to hear it and promised to pay him. Judas began looking for the right chance to betray Jesus.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked him, “Where should we go prepare the Passover meal for you?”
He sent two disciples and told them, “Go into the city. A man carrying a water jar will meet you. Follow him,
“and wherever he goes in, tell the homeowner, ‘The Teacher asks, “Where’s the guest room where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?”’
“He’ll show you a large upstairs room, furnished and ready. Get everything prepared for us there.”
The disciples went into the city and found everything just as Jesus had told them. They prepared the Passover meal.
That evening, Jesus arrived with the twelve.
As they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray me—someone eating with me.”
They were deeply saddened and began asking him one by one, “Surely it isn’t me?”
He answered, “It’s one of the twelve—the one dipping bread with me in the dish.
“The Son of Man goes as Scripture says about him, but how terrible for the one who betrays him! It would have been better for that man if he’d never been born.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. “Take it. This is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them. They all drank from it.
He said, “This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many.
“I’m telling you the truth: I won’t drink the fruit of the vine again until that day when I drink it new in God’s Kingdom.”
After they sang a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus told them, “All of you will fall away tonight because of me. Scripture says, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.’
“But after I’m raised, I’ll go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter said, “Even if everybody else falls away, I won’t.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: today—tonight, before the rooster crows twice—you’ll deny me three times.”
But Peter insisted even more, “Even if I have to die with you, I won’t deny you!” And all the others said the same.
They came to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus told his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
He took Peter, James, and John with him. He began to feel overwhelmed and deeply distressed.
He told them, “My soul is crushed with sorrow, nearly to death. Stay here and keep watch.”
He went a little farther, fell to the ground, and prayed that, if possible, this hour might pass him by.
He said, “Abba, Father, everything is possible for you. Please take this cup away from me. But not what I want—what you want.”
He came back and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Simon, are you asleep? Couldn’t you stay awake for one hour?
“Stay awake and pray so you don’t fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
Jesus went away again and prayed, saying the same words.
When he came back, they were sleeping again; their eyes were so heavy. They didn’t know what to say to him.
He came back a third time and said, “Still sleeping and resting? That’s enough. The hour has come. Look—the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
“Get up. Let’s go. Look, the one betraying me is here.”
Right away, while Jesus was still speaking, Judas arrived—one of the twelve—with a crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, legal teachers, and elders.
The betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The man I kiss is the one. Arrest him and take him away under guard.”
Judas came straight over, saying, “Rabbi! Rabbi!” and kissed him.
Then they grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
One of the people standing there drew a sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
Jesus said to them, “Did you come out to arrest me with swords and clubs, like I’m a robber?
“I was right there with you every day in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me. But this is happening so the Scriptures will be fulfilled.”
Then everyone deserted him and ran away.
A young man had been following Jesus, wearing only a linen cloth over his bare body. The young men grabbed him,
but he left the linen cloth behind and ran off naked.
They led Jesus away to the high priest. All the chief priests, elders, and legal teachers gathered there.
Peter followed Jesus from a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He sat with the guards and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council were looking for testimony against Jesus so they could put him to death, but they couldn’t find any.
Many people gave false testimony against him, but their stories didn’t match.
Some stood up and gave false testimony against him, saying:
“We heard him say, ‘I’ll destroy this temple made by human hands, and in three days I’ll build another one that isn’t made by human hands.’”
But even then, their stories didn’t match.
The high priest stood up in the middle and asked Jesus, “Aren’t you going to answer? What about all these accusations against you?”
But Jesus stayed silent and gave no answer. The high priest asked him again, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
Jesus said, “I am. And you’ll see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with heaven’s clouds.”
The high priest tore his clothes and said, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
“You’ve heard the blasphemy! What’s your decision?” They all judged him deserving of death.
Some began spitting on Jesus. They covered his face, hit him with their fists, and said, “Prophesy!” The guards slapped him too.
Peter was down in the courtyard when one of the high priest’s servant girls came by.
She saw Peter warming himself, looked straight at him, and said, “You were with Jesus from Nazareth too!”
But Peter denied it: “I don’t know or understand what you’re talking about.” He went out onto the entryway, and a rooster crowed.
The servant girl saw him and started telling the people standing there, “This man is one of them.”
Peter denied it again. A little later, the people standing nearby said to him, “You’re definitely one of them—you’re a Galilean, and your accent gives you away.”
Peter began cursing and swearing: “I don’t know this man you’re talking about!”
The rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered Jesus’ words: “Before the rooster crows twice, you’ll deny me three times.” He broke down and wept.
